Subject: Acme load test results + initial sizing note

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Thanks again for running the integration window yesterday — attached are the raw TPS traces and the summarized CSV from our runner. Quick synthesis up front: the workload you sent (mix: 65% short prompt chat, 25% instruction-style, 10% embeddings) hit 970 p95 TPS for single-model runs on your baseline (no KV cache). With Redwood's prefix caching and a 4-GPU pool (A100-equivalent scheduling), we can sustain ~1,250 p95 TPS with median latency ~120ms and p95 latency ~210ms on the same request mix.

Attachments: acme-loadtest-0610.csv (summary), rps_traces_0610.zip (full traces + flamegraphs). I also pushed a dashboard with the run to the link below.

Questions I have for sizing/contract:
- Target p95 TPS you want guaranteed (current ask: 1,000–1,200?)
- Desired commit term (12 vs 24 months) and preferred cadence for reserved capacity billing
- Any hard latency SLOs at p95 or p99 we should guarantee in the SLA

If you want, we can draft a committed-capacity proposal with a few pricing tiers (2x, 4x, 8x GPU pools) and include a ramp credit for the first 3 months. I flagged the runs where prefix caching gives the biggest win — that will affect the unit economics a lot.

Link to run: https://dash.redwood.example/teams/acme/loadtests/0610

Best,

Thanks Connor — the artifacts are super helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our side:

1) The 970 p95 you reported for our baseline matches what we measured on-prem with our earlier runner. The key difference is we do have a 20% tail of longer prompts (20–30 tokens) for fraud-score follow-ups; that inflates p95.

2) Our internal target for go-live is to guarantee 1,000 p95 for core user flows and 1,300 p95 for batch/campaign windows. We can tolerate slightly higher p99 during campaign spikes if you provide a burst policy or auto-scaling fallback.

3) Term: prefer 12 months but open to 24 if economics improve significantly.

4) Pricing: what kind of discount should we expect for a 12-month reserved commit at 4x capacity vs on-demand? Also want to see an option with an initial 3-month ramp where we pay 50% of committed for the ramp.

Can you also confirm whether the p95 numbers you quoted include network egress and typical tokenization overheads (our payloads add ~15% CPU tokenization time)?

Appreciate the quick turn — cc'ing Tom for coverage.

—Sarah
Sr. Engineering Manager, Integrations | Acme Payments

Subject: Re: Acme load test results + initial sizing note — pricing suggestion

Connor — copying the quick recommendation:

- Recommended committed configuration: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved (baseline), with autoscale burst to 6 GPUs for defined campaign windows. That lines up with the 1,250 p95 observed in their runs with prefix caching.

- SLA: Guarantee 1,000 p95 for core flows (monthly measurement) with credits if monthly p95 falls below 95% of target. Exclude third-party network degradations and customer-side tokenization overhead (call this out in SLA exclusions). For campaign windows, offer a "burst guarantee" of 1,300 p95 for 4 cumulative 4-hour windows per month (windows must be scheduled with 48h notice to permit capacity prep); otherwise fallback to best-effort + autoscale.

- Pricing sketch (internal on-demand equivalent = $X/token-hour baseline):
  * On-demand baseline: reference rate (used for comparison)
  * 12-month, 4x reserved: 15% discount off blended on-demand unit economics
  * Ramp model: first 3 months at 50% of committed billing (i.e., customer billed 50% of the normal reserved fee), then reverts to 100% for remainder of term. Add a clause: if actual usage exceeds committed capacity by >25% for 2 consecutive months, revisit commit and true-up.

- Commercial concession cap we can offer without exec sign-off: up to additional 5% (so total 20%). Anything beyond that needs Sales Leader approval.

- Ops note: include a short runbook for scheduled campaign windows (how to request, minimum notice, metrics to monitor). That lowers risk and improves predictability for both sides.

If that looks good I can draft the contract language + SLA snippet.

—Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Subject: Committed capacity proposal (4x) — summary and next steps

Hi Sarah / Tom,

Appreciate the clarifications and the target numbers. Per our internal review here's a concise proposal you can review with finance/infra:

Summary of recommended plan
- Reserved pool: 4x A100-equivalent GPUs (Redwood Dedicated) with autoscale burst to 6x for scheduled campaign windows
- Guaranteed performance: 1,000 p95 for core flows (monthly measurement)
- Burst windows: guarantee up to 1,300 p95 for up to 4 scheduled 4-hour windows per month (48-hour notice required)
- Term & billing: 12 months reserved commit

Commercials (high level)
- 12-month reserved rate: 15% discount vs blended on-demand baseline
- Ramp concession: first 3 months billed at 50% of committed fee to support integration and traffic ramp-up
- True-up clause: if usage > 125% of committed capacity for 2 consecutive months, Redwood and Acme will reconvene to adjust commit (no automatic charges beyond true-up discussion)
- Max discretionary discount without exec approval: extra 5% (total 20%)

SLA & exclusions
- SLA measures monthly p95; credits applied if measured p95 < 95% of target
- Exclusions: third-party network outages, customer-side tokenization delays, and scheduled maintenance communicated per policy

Next steps
1) I attached a more formal proposal PDF (redwood-dedicated-proposal-v2.pdf) with line-item pricing and sample contract language.
2) If the commercial framework is acceptable I'll route for a formal quote and a 30-day DocuSign turnaround for signatures.
3) Ops will schedule a 30-minute kickoff to capture campaign windows and finalize monitoring hooks.

We aimed to size conservatively to avoid repeated true-ups; the attached CSV and traces are the runs we used for the numbers. Let me know if you'd like an alternative 24-month pricing option — that drops the committed price further.

Thanks,
Connor
